blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the executive level, bank guarantees cease to be individual instruments and begin to look like a portfolio. A growing trade business may hold dozens, sometimes hundreds, of active guarantees — performance bonds on running contracts, advance payment guarantees against deposits already received, bid bonds on tenders still in the air, and warranty bonds from projects that ended two years ago but have not yet been formally closed.

What matters at this level is not the detail of any single bond, but the total exposure, the concentration of beneficiaries, the maturity profile, and the cost of maintaining the whole stack inside the banking lines. What surprises many CFOs is how much quiet capacity is tied up in expired or unused guarantees that nobody has formally released.

A regular portfolio review — asking banks to cancel obsolete instruments and pressing beneficiaries to confirm discharge — often frees meaningful capacity with no change in operations. The executive task is to treat guarantees as a living balance sheet of commitments, not a filing cabinet of old paperwork.

items.q: According to the text, what does a bank guarantee become at the executive level?
items.why: "bank guarantees cease to be individual instruments and begin to look like a portfolio."

items.q: What does the text say matters most at the portfolio level?
options: Total exposure, concentration, maturity profile and cost
The wording of each individual bond
The age of the oldest guarantee
The identity of the issuing bank
items.why: "What matters at this level is not the detail of any single bond, but the total exposure, the concentration of beneficiaries, the maturity profile, and the cost…"

items.q: What surprises many CFOs, according to the passage?
options: How cheap new guarantees have become
How much capacity sits trapped in expired or unused guarantees
How rarely banks issue performance bonds
items.why: "how much quiet capacity is tied up in expired or unused guarantees that nobody has formally released."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Freeing capacity need not disrupt day-to-day operations.
Obsolete bonds can quietly consume banking capacity.
A portfolio of guarantees should be reviewed as a whole.
Once issued and filed away, a guarantee needs no further attention.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta justamente contra tratar garantias como papel arquivado — elas exigem revisão contínua.

items.q: The phrase "not a filing cabinet of old paperwork" suggests that guarantees…
options: should be destroyed once contracts end
are best delegated entirely to the legal team
are dead documents with no financial weight
remain live commitments with ongoing balance-sheet impact
items.why: Inferência: opõe "living balance sheet of commitments" a papelada morta — as garantias continuam pesando enquanto não liberadas.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando a primeira revisão de portfólio de garantias em três anos. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. What I'm putting in front of you today is the first proper portfolio-level review of our bank guarantees in three years — and, frankly, it should embarrass us a little.

We went in expecting perhaps ten or fifteen instruments to be reviewed. We found two hundred and thirty-one active guarantees on the banking lines. Of those, forty-eight relate to contracts that closed more than a year ago. Nobody ever asked the banks to cancel them, and nobody chased the beneficiaries to confirm discharge. So they simply sat there, quietly eating into our capacity.

What that means in cash terms is roughly eleven million in headroom we could not use — not because we were trading it, but because the paperwork was never closed. Now, here is what I'm proposing. We run this review every quarter, not every three years. We give one person clear ownership. And whenever a project ends, releasing the guarantee becomes part of closing the contract, not an afterthought.

None of this changes how we operate day to day. It simply stops us paying to carry commitments that ended long ago.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many active guarantees did the review actually find?
items.why: "We found two hundred and thirty-one active guarantees on the banking lines."

items.q: Why had the forty-eight obsolete guarantees remained on the lines?
options: The contracts had not actually ended
Nobody asked the banks to cancel them or chased discharge
Regulation required them to stay open
The banks refused to release them
items.why: "Nobody ever asked the banks to cancel them, and nobody chased the beneficiaries to confirm discharge."

items.q: What does Sophie say the trapped capacity meant in cash terms?
options: Roughly eleven million in unusable headroom
A gain of two hundred million
items.why: "roughly eleven million in headroom we could not use."

items.q: What does Sophie mean when she says it "should embarrass us a little"?
options: The company should have been managing this all along
The bank made an accounting error
The review cost more than expected
The beneficiaries acted in bad faith
items.why: Inferência: o constrangimento é interno — a capacidade estava presa por negligência de processo, não por causa externa.

items.q: Which best captures Sophie's proposed change of approach?
options: Turn portfolio review into a routine with clear ownership
Move all guarantees to a single bank
items.why: Inferência: ela propõe revisão trimestral, um responsável claro e a liberação como parte do fechamento do contrato — rotina, não evento raro.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Treasury tracks the group's total exposure across all outstanding bonds." Here, exposure means…
options: the total risk or amount committed
items.why: Exposure = exposição: o montante total de risco/comprometimento em aberto.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Half the bonds mature in the same quarter, so the ___ is dangerously bunched."
items.why: Maturity profile = perfil de vencimento: como os vencimentos se distribuem no tempo.

items.q: "Three expired bonds were still tying up capacity nobody was using." To tie up capacity means to…
options: lock it away so it cannot be used
items.why: To tie up = imobilizar: prender a capacidade de modo que ela fique indisponível.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Once the client confirms ___, the bank cancels the guarantee and returns the headroom."
items.why: Discharge = liberação: a confirmação formal de que a obrigação foi cumprida e o instrumento pode ser cancelado.

items.q: "A high concentration of beneficiaries is a hidden risk." This refers to…
options: the density of legal clauses in each bond
guarantees spread thinly across many banks
too many guarantees favouring the same few parties
the focus of the treasury team
items.why: Concentration = concentração: muitos instrumentos ligados aos mesmos poucos beneficiários, o que amplia o risco.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em revisões de portfólio e reuniões de tesouraria. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on cancelling the obsolete bonds." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the quarterly review across every business unit." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, unidade por unidade.

items.q: "Two beneficiaries pushed back on the request to confirm discharge." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, relutar — sem necessariamente recusar de vez.

items.q: "Freeing that capacity really moves the needle on our banking headroom." This means it…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir um efeito perceptível.

items.q: "Everyone agreed to chase discharge, but the team never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, não foi levado.
